context:
Goal: the open Duo's tab bar stays readable at every text size, as the web's bar does.
Problem (rule): the fix departs from the web, so you get the final word. A port keeps the web's behaviour, and the web bar has no long press.
Based on (ruling): coordinator, 2026-11-08 08:17 CST: cap the bar labels at the default size, and add the iOS large content viewer.
Based on (read): the web bar's labels are a fixed 10 px (src/app.jsx .mdl-bar button).
Departs from: src/app.jsx:mdl-bar — the web bar has no long press; option a adds the iOS large content viewer, where a long press on a tab shows its name big at accessibility text sizes.
Unvetted: the past-ruling check was not run for this question.
Meanwhile: the lane builds option a on the coordinator's ruling.
home: the Duo bar's decision record, filed by the lane that builds it

options.gain: Readers at large text can still read each tab name.
options.how: At accessibility text sizes, a long press on a tab shows its name big, as iOS does in its own bars.
options.label: Keep the long press
options.lose: It is one behaviour the web does not have.

options.how: The bar's labels stay small at every size, with no long press.
options.label: Drop the long press, to match the web exactly
options.lose: At large text the tab names stay small, with no way to enlarge them.

ref: item 52 (Duo bar at large text, coordinator ruling 2026-11-08 08:17 CST); debt duo-bar-dynamic-type-clips; web src/app.jsx .mdl-bar button
title: Keep the long press that shows a tab's name big on the open Duo? The web bar has none.
why: It is the standard iOS way to read a capped label, and it changes nothing for anyone at normal text sizes.
